title: First saxophones in New Orleans and the Mexican band's Ramis and Lopez
summary: Hazel recalls Remus/Ramis, the Mexican band saxophonist who stayed in the city, and the cornetist Lopez, plus young George Schilling as an early saxophonist.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did he have any saxes in the band in those days?

No, no. In those days there was only one saxophone player in New Orleans. He came here with a Mexican national band, a Mexican government band. His name was Remus. And he came here and although he was an old man at that time, he played with Tony Perranti. But when he originally came here, he was the only saxophone player in New Orleans. And then later on there was a fellow by the name of Dan Sanderson who played saxophone. But in those days, that's far back, they always used clarinets, no saxophones. But the, of the younger generation, but the first one I know of that played saxophone was little George, young George Shilling, Happy Shilling's son. And he started, oh, very, ten, eight, around eleven to twelve years old playing saxophone in his daddy's band. But, uh...

Did you ever hear any more else, anything else about that old Mexican band, your father talked about it? You know, um, um, Jack Lane says his father bought some of the old instruments and some drums from that band for him and some old flags. That's how he got started.

Well, that's, that's, that's possible, that's possible, but, uh, I don't think my dad ever, ever knew anything about that band. The only reason I happened to know about it was, uh, was from old man Ramis himself. Yeah. And that had been several years after he, he'd, uh, settled here with that band. Uh, and, and, and in that band, uh, they had another man who stayed here. Uh, uh, he was, he was, uh, the solo cornetist in this band. His name was Lopez. Oh. He was, uh, sort of on, on, uh, on the art of, uh, this, uh, fellow in New York who's so well-known, makes records and everything.

Del Stegas, that, that, that thing. And he stayed here also, not very long. He stayed here for a couple of years and played in a couple of, I think he played with Happy Schilling. Yeah. And, uh, but he didn't stay around very long. But old man, Ramis, I think, stayed here until he died. And he worked with, with Tony Peretti at the, the Vita there.
What's his name anyway? Full name, do you remember? Ramis?

Uh huh. I wouldn't know, Dick, I wouldn't know he's, he's, he's full. That's the only thing I can remember. Tony could tell, could tell you all about it. Oh yeah. Because he worked with Tony for, for a number of years at that, the Vita.
